definition.name: Control relay
definition.description: A coil operates normally open and normally closed contacts.

terminals.label: A1
terminals.purpose: Coil first connection, paired with A2. Measure across A1–A2 to establish coil demand. This coil circuit is electrically separate from the switched contacts; its pickup/dropout follow the declared voltage thresholds.

terminals.label: A2
terminals.purpose: Coil return connection, paired with A1. Measure across A1–A2 to establish coil demand. This coil circuit is electrically separate from the switched contacts; its pickup/dropout follow the declared voltage thresholds.

terminals.label: COM
terminals.purpose: Common connection of the separate changeover contact. This is a supplied contact circuit, not the coil or a neutral reference.

terminals.label: NO
terminals.purpose: Normally open path from COM: closes when the coil operates and opens on release.

terminals.label: NC
terminals.purpose: Normally closed path from COM: opens when the coil operates and closes on release. It can interrupt a maintained request if wired in that request path.

parts.name: Housing
parts.purpose: The enclosure supports and separates functional parts. This original teaching model is representative equipment, not a manufacturer drawing.

parts.name: Removable cover
parts.purpose: The cover limits access to internal connections. Opening it here is a virtual inspection operation.

parts.name: Terminal clamps
parts.purpose: Metal clamps establish connections to individual conductors. The circuit engine connects terminal IDs, not the apparent proximity of 3D wires.

parts.name: Mounting and fixings
parts.purpose: Mounting hardware supports the equipment. Screws, rail clips and glands are modelled separately from electrical connections.

parts.name: Electromagnetic coil
parts.purpose: Voltage across the coil produces a magnetic operating force. This simulation models coil demand and pickup, rather than magnetic field saturation or inrush.

parts.name: Switching contacts
parts.purpose: Contacts either connect or separate their terminal pairs. Their position is linked to the simulation state, including normally open and normally closed functions.
